plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

interactions.label: Bounding surface
interactions.teaches: Isolating each surface one at a time shows exactly which pieces — top cap, side wall, bottom disk, and the seam where cap meets wall — together enclose the solid whose volume is being integrated

interactions.label: Slice height z

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Starting from the flat disk (x-1)^2 + y^2 = 1 in the xy-plane and then extruding it up to the paraboloid connects the 2D integration region directly to the 3D bounds of the solid

demo_steps.narration: The full solid as in the textbook: the disk (x-1)^2+y^2=1 in the xy-plane is capped above by the paraboloid z=4-x^2-y^2, with the cylinder wall joining them along a closed seam.

demo_steps.title: Highlight the base disk
demo_steps.narration: Isolating the base disk shows the 2D region of integration in the xy-plane — the circle of radius 1 centered at (1,0) that the volume sits above.

demo_steps.title: Raise a horizontal slice
demo_steps.narration: With all surfaces shown, drag the slice plane up: the cross-section inside the cylinder shrinks as the paraboloid closes in, illustrating volume as stacked slices.

demo_steps.title: Flatten to the base region
demo_steps.narration: Switching to 'Base region' removes the cap and wall, leaving the highlighted disk — the xy-domain that the double integral is taken over.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units match the math. Base disk: circle radius 1 centered at (x,y)=(1,0) in the z=0 plane, so it spans x in [0,2], y in [-1,1] and touches the origin. Cylinder wall: vertical surface (x-1)^2+y^2=1 from z=0 up to the paraboloid. Paraboloid cap z=4-x^2-y^2 evaluated over the disk: z=4 at (0,0), z=3 at (1,0), z=2 at (1,±1), z=0 at (2,0); overall scene z in [0,4]. Axes: +z up, +y to the right, +x toward the viewer's lower-left; tick '2' placed at world (2,0,0) on the x-axis. Intersection curve sampled as x=1+cos t, y=sin t, z=4-x^2-y^2 for t in [0,2π]. Colors: paraboloid vertex-color gradient from rim blue #4a90d9 to crown orange #e8632a; cylinder wall translucent blue #5b9bd5 (~0.5 opacity); base disk translucent light blue #9ec9e8 (~0.45); axes and labels black; slice plane translucent teal #2aa198. Slice cross-section = points inside the cylinder with z=h and h <= cap(x,y).
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid and cylinder as parametric BufferGeometry grids with per-vertex colors for the blue-to-orange gradient; keep the cylinder open-ended (no caps) so the hollow top reads correctly. Compute the intersection curve analytically each time the cap or cylinder equation changes. For the equation_input, parse with a safe expression evaluator inside try/catch and show inline parse errors; on success rebuild the cap grid, the cylinder wall (solve the side equation for the radial boundary), the base disk, and the seam curve. The slice plane is a translucent circle clipped to the cylinder footprint and only drawn where h <= cap(x,y); hide it when viewMode is 'Base region'. Use show/hide (not destroy) when toggling surfaces and views so transitions stay smooth.

Finding the volume of a solid with a paraboloid cap and a circular base.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

interactions.label: Bounding surface
interactions.teaches: Isolating each surface one at a time shows exactly which pieces — top cap, side wall, bottom disk, and the seam where cap meets wall — together enclose the solid whose volume is being integrated

interactions.label: Slice height z
interactions.teaches: Dragging a horizontal plane upward reveals the cross-section of the solid at that height; watching the slice area change as z rises makes the volume read as an accumulation of stacked thin disks

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Starting from the flat disk (x-1)^2 + y^2 = 1 in the xy-plane and then extruding it up to the paraboloid connects the 2D integration region directly to the 3D bounds of the solid

interactions.label: Bounded solid
interactions.teaches: Editing the cap formula or the cylinder equation redraws the wall, base disk and paraboloid, showing how the enclosed volume — and hence the integral's value — depends on the bounding surfaces

demo_steps.title: Capped solid (default)
demo_steps.narration: The full solid as in the textbook: the disk (x-1)^2+y^2=1 in the xy-plane is capped above by the paraboloid z=4-x^2-y^2, with the cylinder wall joining them along a closed seam.

demo_steps.title: Highlight the base disk
demo_steps.narration: Isolating the base disk shows the 2D region of integration in the xy-plane — the circle of radius 1 centered at (1,0) that the volume sits above.

demo_steps.title: Raise a horizontal slice
demo_steps.narration: With all surfaces shown, drag the slice plane up: the cross-section inside the cylinder shrinks as the paraboloid closes in, illustrating volume as stacked slices.

demo_steps.title: Flatten to the base region
demo_steps.narration: Switching to 'Base region' removes the cap and wall, leaving the highlighted disk — the xy-domain that the double integral is taken over.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units match the math. Base disk: circle radius 1 centered at (x,y)=(1,0) in the z=0 plane, so it spans x in [0,2], y in [-1,1] and touches the origin. Cylinder wall: vertical surface (x-1)^2+y^2=1 from z=0 up to the paraboloid. Paraboloid cap z=4-x^2-y^2 evaluated over the disk: z=4 at (0,0), z=3 at (1,0), z=2 at (1,±1), z=0 at (2,0); overall scene z in [0,4]. Axes: +z up, +y to the right, +x toward the viewer's lower-left; tick '2' placed at world (2,0,0) on the x-axis. Intersection curve sampled as x=1+cos t, y=sin t, z=4-x^2-y^2 for t in [0,2π]. Colors: paraboloid vertex-color gradient from rim blue #4a90d9 to crown orange #e8632a; cylinder wall translucent blue #5b9bd5 (~0.5 opacity); base disk translucent light blue #9ec9e8 (~0.45); axes and labels black; slice plane translucent teal #2aa198. Slice cross-section = points inside the cylinder with z=h and h <= cap(x,y).
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid and cylinder as parametric BufferGeometry grids with per-vertex colors for the blue-to-orange gradient; keep the cylinder open-ended (no caps) so the hollow top reads correctly. Compute the intersection curve analytically each time the cap or cylinder equation changes. For the equation_input, parse with a safe expression evaluator inside try/catch and show inline parse errors; on success rebuild the cap grid, the cylinder wall (solve the side equation for the radial boundary), the base disk, and the seam curve. The slice plane is a translucent circle clipped to the cylinder footprint and only drawn where h <= cap(x,y); hide it when viewMode is 'Base region'. Use show/hide (not destroy) when toggling surfaces and views so transitions stay smooth.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Toggle bounding surfaces: the paraboloid cap, vertical cylinder, base disk, and their intersection curves highlight one at a time, showing which surfaces enclose the volume.
- Slider for vertical slicing height: the learner moves a horizontal slice upward, the cross-section inside the cylinder appears and shrinks or grows under the paraboloid, showing how accumulated slices form the solid's volume.
- Toggle between base region and capped solid: the learner switches views, the disk (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1 highlights first and then extrudes up to z = 4 - x^2 - y^2, connecting the xy-region to the integration bounds.
- Equation input for the bounded solid: learner edits the cap z = 4 - x*x - y*y and the cylinder (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1; the cylinder wall, base disk, and paraboloid cap redraw to show the new enclosed volume.
